meta.extends_type: lib/cv-screening-types.ts -> Rubric. max_points replaces weight (sum to 100). hard_gatekeepers/hard_caps replace hard_gates. advance_threshold replaces minimum_score_to_advance.
meta.legal_positioning_note: Award and licence references are grounding/scope only. HQ.ai never claims to give employment-law advice. Award pain points describe operational realities a supervisor must run, not legal interpretation.
meta.fairness_note: Legally mandatory licences/checks are ELIGIBILITY gatekeepers assessed post-score as considerations (met/unclear/not_met) - they are never folded into the weighted merit score. A candidate is not less capable because a check is pending. See lib/cv-screening-types.ts deriveConsiderations().

scoring_model.scale: 0-100 merit points. Each role's merit_criteria max_points sum to exactly 100.

criterion_types.ordinal_5: Scored 1-5 against anchors, then mapped to points: points = (score/5) * max_points.
criterion_types.binary_points: Full max_points if the anchor is met, else 0. Used for present/absent signals that ARE merit (e.g. quantified outcomes).

scoring_model.advance_threshold: Default 60/100 to advance to prescreen. Overridable per role.
scoring_model.penalty_overrides: Applied AFTER the weighted merit sum. Negative points for role-specific red flags (e.g. serial <6mo tenure with no project rationale). Never used for protected-attribute proxies; fairness_flag marks criteria where a low score can correlate with caregiving/visa/age and must be read with care.
scoring_model.hard_caps: Eligibility gates. A hard_cap does NOT lower merit - it caps the ADVANCE recommendation and surfaces as a consideration. effect values: 'flag_ineligible' (recruiter confirms work rights/licence before advancing), 'cap_advance:<n>' (capped total until the gate is cleared), 'auto_reject' (reserved for legally cannot-practise cases, e.g. no valid trade licence for licensed electrical work).
scoring_model.how_to_read: merit_total = sum(points) - sum(applicable penalty_overrides). advance = merit_total >= advance_threshold AND no hard_cap is 'auto_reject' AND all mandatory hard_gatekeepers are met-or-unclear (unclear routes to phone screen, not rejection).

award_pain_points: Rostering restrictions and span of ordinary hours (cl. 15, 27): minimum engagement, consecutive-days limits and notice-of-roster-change rules make casual-heavy rosters easy to get wrong.
Penalty rates (cl. 22): evening, weekend and public-holiday loadings differ by day and by employment type; a supervisor must build rosters that stay inside labour budget while covering trade.
Casual loading and casual conversion (cl. 11): 25% loading plus the right-to-request conversion after 12 months is a live obligation that shift-lead managers action, not just HR.

Classification creep (Schedule A): staff doing higher-level duties (keyholding, cash reconciliation, supervising juniors) must be paid at the correct retail level; misclassification is the most common underpayment claim.
Allowances (cl. 19): cold-work, laundry/special clothing and first-aid allowances are frequently missed on payroll.

award_pain_points: Annualised wage arrangements (cl. 24, HIGA): salaried venue staff must be reconciled against what penalty/overtime would have paid - the annual 'better off' reconciliation trips up many operators.
Overtime and penalty rates (cl. 28-29): late-night, weekend and public-holiday loadings on a 7-day trading operation make labour costing a nightly discipline.
Casual employment and minimum engagement (cl. 11): 2-hour minimums and 25% loading against a roster that flexes with covers/bookings.
Broken shifts and split-shift allowances: common in venues with lunch/dinner service; must be structured and paid correctly.
Classification and 'introductory' vs food/beverage/kitchen streams (Schedule A): a cook doing qualified chef work must be classified and paid accordingly.

Minimum engagement for part-time/casual (cl. 12): reception/admin often part-time with minimum-engagement and roster-change rules.
Allowances (cl. 19-20): first-aid and higher-duties allowances missed when staff cover up.

Allowances (cl. 18): first-aid, educational-leader and qualification allowances are frequently missed.
